title: Node OOM & cordon/drain troubleshoot notes
body:
Notes-to-self: incident trace for node(s) hitting OOM + failing to rejoin after drain.

Context:
- Cluster: dev-dedicated-3 (us-west2).
- Provisioning flow: cloud-init -> kubeadm join -> helm post-install hooks.
- Symptom timeline: node reported NotReady -> kubelet OOMKilled repeatedly -> automated cluster-autoscaler retried -> drain/cordon attempted by admin -> node stuck in Terminating pods during drain.

Commands run (raw):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels
  >> node-17   NotReady   <none>   192.168.34.17   <...>
- ssh ubuntu@192.168.34.17 sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager\  
  >> Nov 14 11:07:03 node-17 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
  >> Nov 14 11:07:03 node-17 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2431 (kubelet) score 987 or sacrifice child
- dmesg | grep -i oom
  >> [234567.123456] Killed process 2431 (kubelet) total-vm:120000kB, anon-rss:98000kB, file-rss:2000kB
- ps aux --sort=-rss | head -n 12\  
  >> (on subsequent boot) found containerd-shim processes from failed pods consuming 1.4GiB each (several legacy test pods)
- df -h /var/lib/docker /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/kubelet\  
  >> /var/lib/kubelet  90G  88G  2G  98% <-- suspicious
- ls -lah /var/lib/kubelet/pods | wc -l\  
  >> 1200 (tons of leftover pod dirs)

Quick observations:
- Root cause likely storage exhaustion (inode/disk) on /var/lib/kubelet leading to thrashing and oom. kubelet OOM shows it's killed directly, but multiple container shims persisted and consumed memory.
- Post-install hooks created test workloads that weren't cleaned up (helm job with restartPolicy=Never left stateful remnants?).
- systemd-oomd might be active and propagating kills; verify with systemctl status systemd-oomd.

Hypotheses:
1) Disk pressure on /var/lib/kubelet caused eviction + kubelet memory leak while scanning millions of pod dirs -> OOM.
2) A background job (helm postinstall tests) spawned many pods with high RSS; when they terminated, containerd left shims and processes in zombie-like state.
3) cgroup driver mismatch (docker vs systemd) caused improper accounting and allowed processes to exceed expected memory budgets.

Commands/troubleshooting performed and notes:
- sudo du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/* | sort -h | tail -n 20\  
  >> saw dozens of heavy pod directories (~500MB each) from a failing batch job (helm release: smoke-test-2024-11).
- sudo systemctl status containerd.service\  
  >> active, but many shim processes in D state.
- sudo kill -9 <shim-pid> (iterative) -> freed some memory but not sustainable.
- kubectl drain node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30\  
  >> hung: several pods in Terminating with finalizers; kube-controller-manager couldn't evict because static pods and local storage.
- kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-17
  >> lots of test pods with owners belonging to helm release smoke-test-2024-11.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- cordon node-17 (kubectl cordon node-17) to stop new scheduling.
- On-node cleanup script: stop kubelet, rotate logs, delete stale pod dirs (mv to /tmp/kubelet-orphans-$(date)), restart containerd, restart kubelet.\  
  >> Note: must be careful to avoid deleting live volumes for real stateful workloads. This was run on a dev node.
- Removed helm release smoke-test-2024-11 from Tiller/helm (helm delete --purge) to prevent recreation.

Permanent fixes to propose:
- Add kubelet local disk pressure alert threshold (prometheus alert for NodeDiskRunningOut) and autoscaling policy to cordon/notify earlier.
- Ensure helm post-install smoke tests run in dedicated ephemeral namespace with TTL controller (or kubernetes.io/ttl) so pods get cleaned when job finishes.
- Add cron/cleanup job to GC orphaned pod directories older than X days on dev clusters (but not prod).
- Verify cgroup driver consistency (kubelet config & containerd config) across images. If mismatch, migrate to systemd cgroup driver in containerd and kubelet config.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Why did kubelet get OOM-killed instead of evicting aggressively? Check kubelet eviction thresholds and system oom_score_adj for kubelet process.
- Are there known memory leaks in kubelet version v1.27.3? Check changelog and existing cluster bug reports.
- Confirm if cloud-init hook for smoke tests has runaway loop on failure (retries every minute). If yes, change to exponential backoff.

Repro steps (dev only):
1) Provision small VM (2GB RAM, 30GB root).
2) Run current bootstrap with smoke-test helm release (same chart)
3) Monitor memory/disk with watch (free -m; df -h /var/lib/kubelet) and ps top.
4) When threshold reached, try cordon/drain and observe behaviour of controller-manager and kubelet logs.

Snippets to paste in tickets / Slack when escalating:
- "kubelet OOMKilled on node-17 (us-west2) at 2024-11-14 11:07 UTC. /var/lib/kubelet usage 98%, ~1200 pod dirs, containerd shim processes consuming >6GB total. Suspect helm smoke-test leaving heavy artifacts. JIRA: RINF-1724."

Useful commands for next time (keepers):
- journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo du -sh /var/lib/kubelet/pods/* | sort -rh | head -n 20
- ps auxf | grep containerd-shim | awk '{print $2, $4, $11}' | sort -k2 -nr | head -n 30
- sudo find /var/lib/kubelet/pods -mtime +7 -type d -print | wc -l

Final notes: treat dev clusters as low-trust: run potentially-destructive GC only on dev. For dedicated/prod, instrument with safe TTLs and eviction policies and make smoke tests self-contained (PVCs in ephemeral class, TTL controller).

Logged at: 2024-12-03 by Avery Morales
